cards.claim: In the GDT214 q13 rendering hypothesis, some diagram-local strings may refer into explanatory prose or serve as component/state keys rather than ordinary object names. No particular group, device component or therapeutic content is identified.

scope.unit: Graphical-label register possibility distinct from the balneological genre hypothesis
scope.limits: Historically attested comparator architecture only; Voynich exceptional label/prose reuse prediction is unsupported.

evidence.quote:
This establishes a historically real alternative for q13 graphical text:
some diagram-local strings could function as references into explanatory prose
or as component/state keys, not as ordinary object names.  That alternative is
more compatible with q13's mixed labels/prose and weak one-object ownership
than a naive label dictionary.

It does **not** pass its Voynich prediction.  GDT187 already found that exact
PAGE_HOST reuse between label inventories and same-page prose is sparse but
not exceptional: 57/215 label occurrences appear anywhere in same-page prose,
22/215 at paragraph openings, and the ten-channel adjusted result is
`p=.2963`.  Thus no diagram-to-prose key dictionary has been recovered.

## Updated working theory

The most economical q13 model remains therapeutic balneological records with
an unusually abstract hydraulic/process rendering.  GDT214 adds a distinct
rendering possibility: the graphical-label register may include component or
state references rather than names.  It does not displace GDT210's bath-content
lead because al-Jazari supplies mechanics, not therapeutic content.

No Voynich group is assigned a component, water, wheel, bath, procedure,
figure, or index value.  No direct source relationship, language, plaintext,
or translation follows.  No f84 source, image, annotation, or formal payload
was accessed.

dispositions.reason: AB correctly located preserved source text; its independently assessable graphical-reference hypothesis was not an independently addressed proposition in the broader genre card.

bounded_counterparts.claim: The q13 pages contain therapeutic balneological records with an abstract hydraulic/process representation.
The historical page reading for f82r is: describe the source/apparatus and two or more alternative applications; attach local flow/component labels and reuse OKAL between diagram and prose.
Page-local keys are written beside diagram objects and reused in prose to connect the two channels.
The illustrated page is a therapeutic or hydraulic practical record with component/state arguments.
Main f83r paragraphs carry procedure or state records, while apparatus-local blocks identify components or conduits.

distinctions: Source already quoted is not the same as full proposition represented.
The GDT214 nonnaming component/state reference possibility does not follow from a therapeutic genre, an f82 page model or f83 text-mode split.
The later local-key model has different page coverage and requires a written diagram/prose channel; do not declare equivalence from overlap alone.
This adds an addressable historical hypothesis, not a newly discovered manuscript fact or global novelty verdict.
